text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said it was investigating options trading in TNT Ltd just prior to the A$2.0 billion takeover bid for the transport group by Koninklijke Ptt Nederland NV.
An ASC spokesman told Reuters the issue had been referred to the market watchdog on Thursday afternoon by Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) officials. He said it was too soon to comment further.
An ASX spokesman said the matter was regarded very seriously and its surveillance officials had handed a large number of documents and records relating to the transactions to the ASC.
"ASX surveillance has been investigating what it regards as unusual on-market trade in TNT Ltd options," the spokesman said.
"The trades took place in the period immediately before the formal announcement to the market of the takeover offer for the company," he said.
"The ASX regards this matter as very serious and has today referred it to the Australian Securities Commission," he added.

The managing director of Macquarie Equities Ltd, Warwick Evans, confirmed to Reuters the brokerage firm had been asked by the ASX to provide details of its role in the heavy trading in TNT options late last week.
"We are very relaxed about it and believe there is nothing untoward," Evans said.
He said Macquarie normally accounts for about 35 percent of daily turnover in the options market.
David Poole, an executive director of Macquarie Corporate Finance, which is advising TNT on the agreed takeover bid, said he was not aware of the trading activities of Macquarie Equities.
Both Macquarie Equities and Macquarie Corporate are divisions of Macquarie Bank Ltd.
